A1.justification: Both complete 23-page PDFs describe the same DRAFT framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched, including the renumbered appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original tool-use experiments on ToolBench and RestBench, component ablations, retrieval comparisons and a human documentation evaluation (Tables 1-5).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and human-evaluation results and additionally reports annotator-agreement statistics in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Equations (1)-(5) and the complete prompts in Table 6 retain the same explorer/analyzer/rewriter procedure, diversity constraint and adaptive termination mechanism. Component-notation corrections clarify the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ToolBench I3-Instruction and RestBench-TMDB/Spotify, covering tool use, tool retrieval and documentation quality. No dataset, domain, population or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ReAct, DFSDT and EasyTool, including EasyTool's missing Spotify results. Table 3 retains the same raw-versus-DRAFT documentation comparisons using BM25 and Contriever. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Model choices, thresholds, evaluation metrics and the reported 50-case, three-rater human evaluation remain unchanged. The newly explicit five-iteration maximum and fuller pairwise judging instructions document existing experiments; neither constitutes a reported revision to a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The iteration sweep and cross-model analysis (Figures 6-7), component ablations (Tables 2 and 5), retrieval study (Table 3), and qualitative cases and revision trajectories (Tables 7-12) are unchanged. The existing appendix studies are retained under new section letters.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A introduces Fleiss' kappa reporting for agreement among the existing three human annotators, absent from v1. This adds statistical reliability reporting without documenting additional raters or repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: New Appendix A reports completeness, conciseness and accuracy agreement values of 0.76, 0.71 and 0.72 for RestBench, and 0.77, 0.69 and 0.71 for ToolBench. Existing performance and preference values in Tables 1-5, plotted results and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations (1)-(5) are unchanged. Standardizing component symbols in the prose introduces no new mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about iterative feedback-based documentation refinement, improved tool use and cross-model generalization. No central contribution or claimed scope is substantively revised.

C2.justification: Explanations of cross-model transfer, iteration-related redundancy and overfitting, retrieval improvements and human-comprehension benefits remain unchanged. The added annotator-agreement finding does not introduce a new explanatory argument, applicability boundary or limitation.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 explicitly discloses a maximum of five iterations. New Appendix A provides fuller human-evaluation criteria and describes annotator domain familiarity, selection and compensation. Existing prompts, model identifiers, thresholds and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Chen et al., Friedrich et al., Hong et al., Osiurak and Heinke, and Wieting et al. These support existing motivations concerning tools, exploration and similarity; Section 2.4 newly credits Wieting et al. as inspiration for the existing termination score. Overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording, grammar, terminology and notation edits, updates author/contact information, and adds acknowledgements. A short human-evaluation appendix becomes Appendix A, shifting the previous Appendices A-D to B-E without substantially reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2 correct 'Trail' to 'Trial', Figure 2 gains caption clarification, and Table 1's caption is shortened and corrected. Conference running headers and local layout shifts are added. All seven figures and twelve tables are retained without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: v1 reports human preferences without annotator-agreement statistics or detailed judging criteria; v2 Appendix A supplies both, making that evidence easier to assess. The explicit iteration cap, clearer notation and improved attribution also aid reproducibility and clarity. These are useful, limited improvements to an otherwise unchanged method and empirical contribution.
